grammar.title: 3B: Articles - a / an, the, no article
grammar.explanation:
Use **a** or **an** with a singular countable noun when you say what something is. Say **an** before a vowel sound: **a charger**, **an old keyboard**.

Use **a / an** the first time you mention something new, like **a notification** or **an update**. Later, when both people know which one you mean, use **the**: **the notification**, **the update**.

Use **the** when there is only one of something, or when the meaning is clear. For example: **the battery** of your phone, **the software** on this device.

Use **the** with superlatives and with places in town. For example: **the fastest download**, **the bank**.

Use **a / an** in What...! exclamations and in expressions of frequency. For example: **What a useful device!**, **twice a week**.

Use **no article** when you talk about things in general with plural or uncountable nouns. For example: **Passwords** are important, and **backups** keep your files safe.

Use **no article** with **home**, **work**, **school** after **at / to / from**. For example: **at home**, **from work**.

Also use **no article** before meals, days, and months. For example: **for lunch**, **on Friday**.

Use **no article** before **next / last** + day, week, or month. For example: **next week**, **last month**.
examples: I bought *a charger* for my new phone.
She found *an old keyboard* in the garage.
I got *a notification* from my bank this morning.
I read *the notification* on the train.
*The battery* of this phone lasts all day.
*The software* on my device is very fast.
That was *the fastest download* I have ever seen.
What *a useful device*! I take it everywhere.
*Passwords* must be long and difficult to guess.
She stayed *at home* and watched a film.
I always keep *a backup* of my photos.
